newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: SKB Banka rating raised to BBB+ - Thomson.
newsitem.headline: SKB Banka rating raised to BBB+ - Thomson.

text.p: Bank rating agency Thomson BankWatch-Bree said on Monday it had upgraded the long term senior debt rating of Slovenia's bank SKB Banka to BBB+ from BBB.
"The new rating is among the highest in the region of the Central and Eastern Europe and reflects SKB's favourable performance," Ramin Habibi, president of the agency, told Reuters.
He said SKB was the best rated among Slovenia's banks, followed by state-owned Nova Kreditna Banka Maribor with a long-term rating of BBB-.
"Our rating reflects SKB's innovative and capable management, its stategic position in Slovenian banking, as well as profitability and underlying capital concerns," the agency said in a statement.
It said SKB's short-term local currency rating remained uchanged at LC-1 on a par with Nova Kreditna Banka Maribor and Nova Ljubljanska Banka.
SKB is Slovenia's leading private sector bank, and the second largest bank in the country with a market share of 11.3 percent.

The bank is poised to become the first Slovenian company to be listed abroad when its global depository receipts (GDRs), representing up to 29 percent of SKB's equity, are due to be listed on the London stock exchange later this week.
